newsitem.title: JAPAN: G7 to confirm previous forex stance in Denver--MOF.
newsitem.headline: G7 to confirm previous forex stance in Denver--MOF.

text.p: The Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations will confirm the previous agreement on foreign exchange markets they reached in April at their June 20-22 summit in Denver, Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told reporters on Tuesday.
Asked whether currencies would be an issue at the summit and whether the G7 would issue a statement on the foreign exchange markets, Mitsuzuka said:
"I think we will be confirming what was decided at the G7 finance minister's meeting in Washington."
He said the government would like to draft a bill covering the restructuring of fiscal finances in time for the next parliamentary session, which is widely expected to be convened in September.

Asked about news on Monday that Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd and Barclays Bank have agreed to discuss several areas of cooperation, the minister said this was something that came about as part of Japan's movement toward financial market reform.
He added that more such tie-ups were likely to happen in the future.

Asked about a media report on Tuesday morning saying that the tax panel of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party believes Japan's securities transaction tax should be abolished in fiscal 1999/00 at the latest, Mitsuzuka said this was something the government's tax panel would have to discuss.
